why: The forbidden-path rule, pinned as cases. A rule that only exists in a postmortem is a rule that waits for the next incident; these cases are the rule's executable form, and they must fail BEFORE the fix that adds them.

cases.why: The runtime configuration file. Its values are the vault pepper and API tokens; it was committed in 16 commits between 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-15 and the published history had to be rewritten on 2026-11-26.
The same file with a different name is the same secret.
The rule is about the file name in any directory, not only at the repository root.
The template carries no values, and the repository carries it on purpose: it is how the operator learns which keys exist.
The vault's own state file never enters the repository.
The rule matches the file name in any directory.
A tier-2 passphrase never enters the repository, under any name.
The rule matches the suffix in any directory.
The GitHub personal access token never enters the repository.
The rule matches the file name in any directory.
Build output is not repository content.
Source is what the repository is for.
A document named dist is not under the dist directory; the rule is about directories.
The rule's own owner is repository content.
